title: Circle
tagline: Community service marketplace connecting requesters with providers through dual Flutter apps.
overview: Circle connects people who need small services done with providers ("captains") who can do them, following the same dual-app pattern as Qareeb but focused on general services rather than delivery specifically.
problem: There was no structured way for people to request and offer small local services, with trust and coordination happening informally through word of mouth.
solution: Two focused Flutter apps — one for requesting services, one for providers accepting and completing them — with a shared request/status lifecycle between them.
architecture: BLoC-based Flutter apps with a request state machine shared conceptually between both apps, covering creation, acceptance, in-progress, and completion states.
features: Service request creation with category and details
Provider-side browsing and acceptance of nearby requests
Status tracking through the full request lifecycle
Separate, role-specific interfaces for requesters and providers
challenges: Designing a request lifecycle general enough to cover many service types without becoming vague
Building trust signals into the flow so both sides felt confident engaging with strangers
lessonsLearned: General-purpose marketplace apps need clearer status communication than specialized ones, since users can't assume shared expectations
futureImprovements: Rating and review system for providers
In-app messaging between requester and provider
results: Working dual-app marketplace covering the full request-to-completion flow
